you: Used instead of the name of the person being spoken to; it is a second-person pronoun.
You have to be at least 18 years old to see that film.
Used before a word that means the person or people someone is talking to.
young: If you are young, you have not lived a long time.
She was only a young girl.
A young is an offspring of an animal.
The lion caught a gnu to feed its young.
your: Your things are things which belong to you.
Can I eat some of your ice-cream please?
yours: If something is yours, it belongs to you.
Excuse me, is this yours? I found it on the desk.
yourself: You use yourself when the person doing an action and receiving an action are both you.
Don't pretend you don't know. You yourself have seen these kinds of problems.
If you do something by yourself, you do it alone.
That's beautiful, son. Did you make it by yourself?
If you don't feel yourself, you are different from usual, because you are sick, scared, stressed, etc.
yourselves: You use yourselves when the people doing an action and receiving an action are both you.
Be careful children. You'll hurt yourselves.
Don't pretend you don't know. You yourselves have seen these kinds of problems.
If you do something by yourselves, you do it alone.
That's beautiful, boys. Did you make it by yourselves?
If you don't feel yourself, you are different from usual, because you are sick, scared, stressed, etc.
youngster: A youngster is young person, someone who is not an adult. Usually this means a child, but sometimes can mean an adolescent or a baby.
yo: Yo, man, how have you been lately?
Yo, dude! What was that for?
Yo' mama's so fat they filmed 'Gorillas in the Mist' in her shower.
youth: The quality or state of being young.
The part of life after childhood.
york: York is a city in England.
yo-yo: A yo-yo is a toy that spins and goes up and down, hanging from a string.
Let's go play with my yo-yo.
yolk: The yolk is the yellow part of an egg.
youngish: In spite of his youngish appearance, he had done much.
yogurt: Yogurt is a creamy, white food that is made when bacteria is added to milk.
yoshi: Yoshi is a Japanese male given name.
yoghurt: Yoghurt is a creamy, white food that is made when bacteria is added to milk.
yodel: If you yodel, you sing in a way that quickly alternates between your regular voice and a very high voice.
The Swiss think they invented yodeling, but it's used in many cultures.
yodeller: A yodeller is a person who yodels.
yodeler: A yodeler is a person who yodels.
youthful: A youthful person is an older person who seems young.
The young man was being very youthful.
yoke: n
A yoke is a wooden frame or bar with loops or bows at either end, used for joining two oxen or other animals together to pull a plough or vehicle.
The farmer used a yoke to connect the oxen.
n
If someone has to live under the yoke of something bad, they have to lives that are controlled by it.
The people struggled to free themselves from the yoke of slavery.
n
A yoke is something that connects two parts and keeps them together.
The yoke of marriage binds two people together.
n
In engineering, a yoke is a crosspiece that connects two parts of a mechanism.
The yoke of the airplane controls its pitch and roll.
n
A yoke is a fitted part of a garment, usually around the neck and shoulders, that provides support and shape.
The dress had a lace yoke around the neckline.
v
If you yoke animals, such as oxen, to something that they pull, you put a yoke on them, so they can pull it.
The farmer yoked the oxen to the plough.
v
If you yoke two things together, you join or link them together closely.
The new policy yokes education with economic development.
v
If someone is yoked to something bad, they have to lives that are controlled by it.
The workers felt yoked to their desks.
youthfully: If something is done youthfully, it is done in a youthful way.
yoga: A group of exercises from India that include stretching, breathing, and relaxing.
She practices yoga every morning to relax and stay fit.
A way of thinking and living that helps people feel calm and healthy.
yokohama: Yokohama is a city and seaport to the south of Tokyo, Japan.
